blocks.text: The relationships between genes and DNA are best understood by mutation studies. You have studied about mutation and its effect in Chapter  4.  Effects of large deletions and rearrangements in a segment of DNA are easy to comprehend.  It may result in loss or gain of a gene and so a function.  The effect of point mutations will be explained here.  A classical example of point mutation is a change of single base pair in the gene for beta globin chain that results in the change of amino acid residue glutamate to valine. It results into a diseased condition called as sickle cell anemia. Effect of point mutations that inserts or deletes a base in structural gene can be better understood by following simple example.
